$comment: CANONICAL PQL vocabulary. Single source of truth for ALL parsers (JS: webapp/internal/webui/www/pql.js; Go: cli-go/pkg/pql; TS: discovery-service/core/pql.ts). Each parser embeds/loads this file so the grammar can never drift. The spec prose lives in docs/general/pql.md; this file is the machine-readable form. Golden fixtures that all three parsers assert against: docs/general/pql-golden.jsonl.
$relations_comment: from = authored-by (actor axis). about = concerns/targets (involved axis; maps to the DS involvedDomain filter). Exactly one relation per sentence. On a tenant the relation+scope clause is optional and defaults to (from, @<tenant>).
$types_comment: User-facing alias -> internal value. Only messages->dms is remapped; the rest pass through. The type slot ALSO accepts a fully-qualified event type matching event_type_pattern (e.g. pub.polis.follow.announced) for operational precision; FQ types pass through verbatim as the internal value.
$event_type_sets_comment: Expansion of view aliases to the DS stream event types they cover (used by discovery-service pqlToStreamQueryFilters). activity = [] means no type filter (all events). drafts/messages are owner-local and not DS-resolvable, so they have no expansion.
$scope_atoms_comment: Multi-token scope phrases -> internal value. Order matters when atoms share a leading token. Bare handles (FQDN matching handle_pattern) -> @<handle>. Possessive form <handle>'s network -> @<handle>:network.
$first_person_comment: SCOPE-RESOLUTION BOUNDARY. These owner-relative scopes are resolvable ONLY by the webapp/auth API against the authenticated owner. The DS dispatcher REJECTS them (400 PQL_OWNER_RELATIVE_UNSUPPORTED) and the webapp rejects them for anonymous visitors. The grammar still PARSES them everywhere; this is a per-surface dispatch policy, not a grammar fork.
